questions.q: What is the ultimate source of energy for almost all ecosystems on Earth?
a: Light energy from the Sun
Geothermal heat from Earth's core
Chemical energy in deep sea vents
Nuclear energy from fossil fuels

questions.q: What is a producer defined as in an ecosystem?
a: An animal that eats other organisms
An organism that makes its own organic nutrients using energy from sunlight (photosynthesis) or chemical reactions
A fungus that breaks down dead organic matter
A herbivore that feeds exclusively on grass

questions.q: What is a consumer defined as?
a: A plant that produces glucose
A decomposer that recycles minerals
An organism that gets its energy by feeding on other organisms
An inorganic mineral salt in the soil

questions.q: What is a food chain?
a: A complex network of interconnected feeding relationships
The total dry mass of organisms in a habitat
The chemical recycling of nitrogen in soil
A chart showing the transfer of energy from one organism to the next, beginning with a producer

questions.q: What does a food web represent?
a: A network of interconnected food chains showing all the feeding relationships in an ecosystem
A single linear path of energy flow
The number of predators in a specific habitat
The migration routes of birds

questions.q: What is a trophic level defined as?
a: The geographical location of an organism
The position of an organism in a food chain, food web, or pyramid of biomass
The total population size of a species
The rate of respiration in an animal

questions.q: Why is energy transferred between trophic levels inefficient, with roughly 90 percent of energy lost at each step?
a: Energy is created continuously by consumers
Predators eat all available prey completely
Energy is lost through respiration, movement, heat, excretion, and uneaten body parts
Plants absorb all sunlight perfectly without loss

questions.q: What is a pyramid of numbers used to show?
a: The total dry mass of organisms at each trophic level
The total energy content in kilojoules
The rate of reproduction of herbivores
The number of individual organisms at each trophic level in a food chain

questions.q: What is a pyramid of biomass?
a: A chart showing the total dry mass of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain
A count of the number of plants in a forest
The measurement of water volume in a lake
The rate of carbon dioxide uptake

questions.q: What role do decomposers (such as bacteria and fungi) play in an ecosystem?
a: They produce oxygen via photosynthesis
They break down dead organic material and waste, releasing mineral nutrients back into the soil
They act as apex predators
They consume primary producers directly

questions.q: What is population defined as in ecology?
a: All the different species living in a particular habitat
The non-living physical factors of an environment
A group of organisms of one species living in the same area at the same time
The global sum of all ecosystems

questions.q: What is a community defined as?
a: A single organism surviving in isolation
The non-living climate factors of a region
The Earth's atmosphere and oceans combined
All of the populations of different species living in a particular habitat or ecosystem

questions.q: What is an ecosystem defined as?
a: A unit containing all of the organisms (community) and their environment (abiotic factors) interacting together
Only the living animal populations in a region
The chemical elements cycling through soil
The weather patterns of a continent

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an abiotic factor in an ecosystem?
a: Predatory lions
Light intensity, temperature, moisture, and soil pH
Parasitic worms
Herbivorous insects

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a biotic factor?
a: Soil pH levels
Rainfall volume
Competition between individuals for food, predation, or disease
Oxygen concentration in water

questions.q: What is the primary role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the nitrogen cycle?
a: To convert nitrates into nitrogen gas
To break down animal protein into urea
To absorb sunlight for plants
To convert inert nitrogen gas from the atmosphere into nitrates or ammonia that plants can use

questions.q: What do nitrifying bacteria do in the soil?
a: Convert ammonium compounds into nitrites and then into nitrates, which plants absorb
Convert nitrates into nitrogen gas
Decompose dead leaves into water
Absorb carbon dioxide from the air

questions.q: What is the function of denitrifying bacteria in the nitrogen cycle?
a: To supply nitrogen to plant roots
To convert soil nitrates back into nitrogen gas, releasing it into the atmosphere
To turn glucose into protein
To kill harmful soil pathogens

questions.q: How does carbon enter the biotic components of an ecosystem from the atmosphere?
a: Through animal respiration
Through the combustion of fossil fuels
Through photosynthesis by green plants fixing carbon dioxide into organic molecules
Through root absorption of carbonate rocks

questions.q: Which processes return carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere in the carbon cycle?
a: Photosynthesis and transpiration
Nitrogen fixation and lightning
Precipitation and condensation
Respiration of organisms, decomposition by microorganisms, and combustion of fossil fuels

questions.q: Why are food chains usually limited to a maximum of 4 or 5 trophic levels?
a: Energy losses at each trophic level are so large that there is insufficient energy remaining to support further trophic levels
Apex predators refuse to eat tertiary consumers
There is a shortage of water in ecosystems
Plants stop producing oxygen

questions.q: What is biodiversity defined as?
a: The number of non-living rocks in a habitat
The number of different species that live in an area and the genetic variation within them
The rate of energy flow through a food web
The total mass of herbivores in a biome

questions.q: What is the term for an organism that hunts, kills, and eats other animals?
a: Prey
Producer
Predator
Decomposer

questions.q: What is the animal that is hunted and eaten by a predator called?
a: Apex consumer
Secondary producer
Parasite
Prey

questions.q: Which of the following organisms occupies the first trophic level in almost all terrestrial food chains?
a: Green plants (producers)
Herbivorous insects
Carnivorous mammals
Fungi and bacteria

questions.q: What does a pyramid of energy typically look like compared to a pyramid of numbers?
a: It can be inverted or diamond-shaped
It is always a true upright pyramid because energy is always lost at each successive trophic level
It is completely flat
It increases in width at higher trophic levels

questions.q: What is a habitat defined as?
a: The role an organism plays in an ecosystem
The entire planet Earth
The place where an organism lives
The chemical composition of soil

questions.q: Which of the following describes mutualism?
a: A relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
An interaction where both organisms are harmed
Competition between two species for identical resources
A relationship between two organisms of different species where both benefit (e.g., nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume root nodules)

questions.q: What is an example of parasitism?
a: A tapefish or tick living on or inside a host organism, obtaining nutrients at the host's expense
Bees pollinating flowering plants
Remora fish attaching to sharks for transport without harm
Two lions fighting over territory

questions.q: What is the role of lightning in the nitrogen cycle?
a: It creates carbon dioxide in the air
It provides high enough energy to cause nitrogen and oxygen in the atmosphere to react, forming nitrogen oxides that dissolve in rain
It destroys soil bacteria
It converts glucose into starch in leaves

questions.q: What is an apex predator?
a: An organism that eats only plants
The first producer in a food chain
A predator at the top of a food chain with no natural predators of its own
A microscopic decomposer

questions.q: How do saprotrophic microorganisms (decomposers) obtain their nutrients?
a: By performing photosynthesis in sunlight
By hunting live prey in packs
By absorbing mineral ions from rocks directly
By secreting extracellular enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbing the digested products

questions.q: What happens to the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere during daylight hours in a well-forested area?
a: It decreases due to active photosynthesis by trees
It increases rapidly due to plant respiration
It remains completely unchanged
It turns into liquid oxygen

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a trophic level?
a: The speed at which an animal moves
The feeding level or step an organism occupies in a food chain
The depth of soil where roots grow
The temperature range of a habitat

questions.q: What is the main reason why energy transfer is inefficient along a food chain?
a: Animals eat too quickly
Plants absorb excess light
Much of the energy ingested is lost as metabolic heat during respiration, excreted as waste, or locked in uneaten body parts
Decomposers destroy energy

questions.q: Which of the following cycles relies heavily on both photosynthesis and respiration to maintain balance?
a: Water cycle
Nitrogen cycle
Phosphorus cycle
Carbon cycle
